title: The Donor
scenario:
Elena is dying of liver failure. Her brother Marco is the only compatible living donor. He offers a lobe of his liver, which will save her life, but he sets one condition: she must first tell their elderly mother the truth about the fire that killed their father twenty years ago. Elena caused it, by accident, as a teenager. Marco took the blame to protect her, and their mother has grieved him as a reckless boy ever since.

Marco says he has carried the lie long enough, and that he cannot give his sister his body while she lets their mother die believing a falsehood about him. Elena says the truth would shatter their mother in her final years, and that Marco is using a scalpel to force a confession.

Without the surgery, Elena dies within months. With it, their mother learns what her daughter did.
question: Should Elena meet his condition?
option_a_text: She should tell the truth. Marco has a right not to give his own flesh while remaining a scapegoat, and their mother deserves to know her son.
option_b_text: She should refuse. A life-saving gift extracted by ultimatum is coercion, and sparing a frail old woman needless anguish is its own duty.
